data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word ‘tarsos’ meaning ‘stone’ or ‘rock’. In the Bible, Tarsion could refer to various places, such as the city of Tarsus, where Paul was born, or the name of a stone or rock.

in_greek.name: Ταρσίων
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ταρσίων προέρχεται από την πόλη Ταρσού, στην Κιλικία, και συσχετίζεται με την περιοχή της Κιλικίας. Ο Ταρσίων ήταν ένας από τους σπουδαίους μαθητές του Αποστόλου Παύλου και είχε ένα ιδιαίτερο ρόλο στην εκκλησία της Κιλικίας. Το όνομα του Ταρσίων συνδέεται επίσης με την ιδιότητα του αποστόλου και της αποστολικής αποστολής.

in_latin.name: Tarsion
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Tarsionem a civitate Tarsus, in Cilicia, ortam derivatur et cum regione Ciliciae associatur. Tarsion unus ex discipulis Apostoli Pauli et in ecclesia Ciliciae functus est. Nomen Tarsionis cum apostolatus et apostolicae missionis officio connectitur.

in_english.name: Tarsion
in_english.meaning: from Tarsus, a city of Cilicia, Tarsion, a disciple of Apostle Paul
in_english.long_meaning: The name Tarsion originates from the city of Tarsus in Cilicia, and is associated with the region of Cilicia. Tarsion was one of the esteemed disciples of Apostle Paul and played a unique role in the church of Cilicia. The name Tarsion is also connected with the apostolate and the apostolic mission.

data.cultural_impact: In the Christian context, the name "Tarsion" connotes a strong foundation or steadfastness, as a reminder of Christ's teachings to build our lives on the rock of faith. It can also represent a commitment to stand firm in our beliefs and values, just as a solid rock withstands the test of time.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Tarsion" holds deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes the Rock of Ages, Jesus Christ, upon whom we can securely build our lives. It is a reminder of the biblical promise that He is our solid foundation, and when we trust in Him, we will never be moved. This name can be a source of inspiration for those seeking stability and resilience in their spiritual journey.

historical_references.reference: Tarsius, the legendary founder of Tarsus, was a Hittite prince who supposedly converted to Christianity and was martyred for his faith. According to tradition, he was the son of King Tarcondemus of Cilicia and was sent to Rome to be educated. There, he was converted to Christianity by the apostles Peter and Paul. After returning to Tarsus, he was persecuted for his faith and was eventually killed by the Romans in the late 1st or early 2nd century.
historical_references.context: Legendary founder of Tarsus, converted to Christianity and martyred for his faith
